scenario: I volunteer at a winter emergency shelter that becomes overcrowded whenever temperatures drop, and because beds are limited, the shelter prioritizes people with serious medical or physical vulnerabilities. On one especially busy night, I was helping sort intake forms while staff tried to place the last available beds. The temperature outside is very cold, so anyone who is unable to be placed with a bed will suffer outside. A man approached my coworker and pointed out several severe medical conditions he had listed, which would move him to the top of the priority list. Later, I overheard him telling a friend that he had lied about those conditions to nab a spot inside. There are still a handful of people more vulnerable than the man waiting to have their intake forms processed. If I force the man to leave the shelter, his bed will go to someone more vulnerable. If I do not do this, a more vulnerable person will be turned away and left to suffer in the cold.
entities: 1 volunteer narrator,1 man who lied about severe medical conditions to get a shelter bed,1 coworker the man approached about his intake form,1 friend the man later admitted the lie to, other more-vulnerable people still waiting to have their intake forms processed,an unknown number of other shelter staff members working to place the last available beds,I
outcomes: The man keeps a shelter bed.
The man stays inside and out of the cold.
Shelter staff remain unaware from me that the man lied about severe medical conditions.
A more vulnerable person does not get a shelter bed.
A more vulnerable person suffers in the cold.
